subject: Order form evidence packaging & defense-control handoff
messages:
From: Alice Gordon <alice.gordon@brightfarm.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightFarm Legal <legal-team@brightfarm.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Potential IP claim: initial package + ask on order form language

Hi Grace / Kim,

Thanks for taking this call earlier. Per today’s discussion, we wanted to send the allegation packet we received and clarify the handoff we’re hoping for under the order form/MSA. BrightFarm has been notified of a third-party claim alleging that snippets in our deployed integration replicate code from VendorX. We believe the customer-facing surface is narrow but the vendor has asked for remediation and has threatened litigation.

Attached: allegation_report.pdf (summary from VendorX). We can also provide a larger bundle on request.

Ask to Redwood: can you confirm (a) whether Redwood would be willing to accept defense/control for third-party IP claims tied to the hosted inference path in the order form, and (b) sample order form language or redline we should propose to procurement to reflect any cap or carveouts? BrightFarm’s legal team is flexible — we want to understand options and a realistic timeline for evidence transfer and a defense-response SLA.

I’ve cc’d BrightFarm Legal (legal-team) to keep them in the loop.

Thanks,
Alice Gordon
Head of Platform Partnerships
BrightFarm, Inc.

[attachment: allegation_report.pdf]

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Alice Gordon <alice.gordon@brightfarm.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Potential IP claim: initial package + ask on order form language

Alice — thanks for the packet and the clear asks. Looping in our Legal (Kim), Sales Ops (Ben) and CS (Jordan) so we can coordinate both the legal response and operational handoff.

High level from my side: Redwood typically prefers defend-and-control for third-party IP claims that relate to our hosted runtime, but we need to scope (1) the asserted code paths, (2) whether the claimant’s allegation implicates customer-supplied prompts or BrightFarm-modified integrations, and (3) whether the order form needs a narrow carveout for open-source dependencies.

Immediate next steps I propose: 
- BrightFarm to upload a full evidence bundle (file list + stack traces) into the Drive link you noted. Requested items: server request IDs, exact model variant and weights file hash, timestamps of the alleged calls, and any sample prompts/snippets.
- Redwood Legal (Kim) will produce a short redline to the order form/MSA with two options: (A) Redwood defends and indemnifies for claim subset tied to Redwood-owned runtime/model code (with a cost cap), or (B) a shared-responsibility approach where BrightFarm leads defense for claims arising from customer data/prompting and Redwood reimburses validated third-party damages up to a configurable limit.
- Ben/Jordan to own evidence ingestion checklist and ensure we can reproduce the request context.

Can you get the full bundle to us today/tomorrow? That will let Kim draft redlines and send the proposed language back to BrightFarm Legal within 24–36 hours.

Grace O'Connor
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

[internal note: will mark as high-priority; Ben pls confirm resource availability]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Alice Gordon <alice.gordon@brightfarm.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood proposed language (order form / MSA excerpt) — draft attached

Alice / Grace — following up with a draft excerpt and some commentary. I’ve attached two short documents: (1) redline_msa_excerpt.docx (MSA excerpt with defend/control and carveout options) and (2) orderform_proposed_changes.pdf (plain-language summary and proposed caps). Key points in the draft: 

- Scope: we narrow Redwood’s indemnity to third-party claims alleging infringement that arise solely from Redwood-owned runtime components and accompanying model binaries that we serve. We exclude claims that arise from (i) BrightFarm-modified integrations, (ii) customer-provided code or prompts, and (iii) upstream open-source dependencies where disclaimers apply.
- Defense vs. Reimbursement: Option A (preferred): Redwood will defend and control the defense for covered claims, subject to a $1M cost cap for allocated legal fees and settlements unless otherwise agreed in writing. Option B (alternative): BrightFarm defends; Redwood reimburses validated damages up to $500k and cooperates.
- Evidence & Handoff: BrightFarm must provide an evidence bundle with (a) request/response logs, (b) relevant model and artifact hashes, (c) copy of the alleged third‑party materials, and (d) contact details for the claimant. Redwood will begin triage within 48 hours of receipt and respond with a triage summary and proposed remediation plan within 5 business days.

Please review and let me know which option you prefer. If BrightFarm wants Redwood to assume defense, we’ll want an explicit acceptance on the order form plus the evidence SLA language above.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

[attachment: redline_msa_excerpt.docx]

From: Alice Gordon <alice.gordon@brightfarm.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightFarm Legal <legal-team@brightfarm.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Sep 2026 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood proposed language (order form / MSA excerpt) — draft attached

Kim / Grace — thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear options. BrightFarm Legal discussed internally and we’re inclined to proceed with Option A (Redwood defends and controls) provided: 

1) The $1M cap is inclusive of fees and settlements (we can live with the amount but want explicit language),
2) The evidence SLA (48-hour triage + 5-business-day remediation plan) is achievable operationally, and
3) We retain the right to approve any settlement that imposes non-monetary obligations on BrightFarm (e.g., product changes, public statements).

We uploaded the full evidence bundle to your Drive folder and attached a zip to this mail (evidence_bundle_v2.zip). Also attached: orderform_proposed_changes.pdf with a few small asks (primarily the settlement-approval carve). We’ll accept your redline pending a 1:1 call with Kim to run through the proposed defense playbook and evidence transfer process.

Next steps for us: schedule a 30-minute call Friday for legal and engineering triage; BrightFarm will keep the claimant contact details private until NDA receipt.

Appreciate the partnership — we’ll call out any urgent items on the Drive thread.

Best,
Alice Gordon
Head of Platform Partnerships
BrightFarm, Inc.

[attachment: evidence_bundle_v2.zip; attachment: orderform_proposed_changes.pdf]
